title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：sacrifice　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sacrifice 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the counsellor ① made the sacrifice that no listener in the garden would have counted, and he said the making was the whole of the evening. The ② sacrifice, meaning the offering itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed uncounted in the book; sacrifice, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ bit of sacrifice in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ sacrifice at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Sacrifice, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the counsellor said the counting is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sacrifice was the whole of the matter, meaning the love and not the offering. The ⑥ sacrifice, meaning the love and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; sacrifice, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both offering and a love. He said the love is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ sacrifice had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ sacrifice of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of counting; sacrifice, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sacrifice I remember is the sacrifice counted in the journal, which closed in 1960 and is still counted as the quietest in the garden. ⑩ Sacrifice, my mother said in 1962, is the only thing that improves by being counted; all sacrifice, she said, is a love that has agreed to look like offering. She said the love was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 牺牲；奉献（指小园里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 牺牲；奉献（指那份牺牲本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the sacrifice 作出这一份牺牲
D. n. 牺牲；奉献（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 牺牲之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的牺牲之事）
F. n. 牺牲；奉献（指心记里写到、被清点的那一份）
G. n. 牺牲、付出（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 付出（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the sacrifice that no listener in the garden would have counted
The sacrifice, meaning the offering itself and not the letter
Every bit of sacrifice in that garden
the sacrifice at the far bench
the sacrifice was the whole of the matter
the sacrifice had become a line in a journal
The sacrifice of the whole thing

answers.why: make the sacrifice 意为“作出这一份牺牲”，1953 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯清点的一份牺牲做了一遍。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲；奉献”，指那份牺牲本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被清点。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲；奉献”，指小园里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲；奉献”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲、付出”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份付出就是那件事的全部。
sacrifice 意为“付出”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份牺牲，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲；奉献”，指心记里写到、被清点的那一份，到 1958 年这一份成了心记里的一行。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的牺牲之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的清点。
sacrifice 意为“牺牲；奉献”，我记得的是心记里清点过的那一份，1960 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一份。
sacrifice 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，牺牲是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的牺牲。
